properties.description:
A restructuring is safe exactly when function is provably preserved — and nothing computes that, so today it can only be asserted

*Anthony chose this, 2026-08-02, as the first step under [BL-179] / dec:maturity-restructuring-delta — of the two offered (this, or fork-and-measure on the 14 seams).* The invariant, from the decision: a maturity restructuring holds the function set INVARIANT and moves everything else, so it is safe exactly when no Capability was added or removed, no Requirement was added or removed, and no SATISFIES edge changed — only ALLOCATED_TO / CONTAINS / Interface edges moved. Why it is buildable now rather than invention: compare_designs already diffs two as-designed records at node and edge granularity, directionally and deterministically; what is missing is the classification that turns a diff into a verdict. The move it makes is dec:passing-is-verified's, applied to structure — the difference between a refactor someone hopes is safe and one the graph checked. Where it must not cheat, and this is the whole risk: a classifier with a hidden inclusion list would call a divergence it does not recognise "structural" and certify a design it never examined — [BL-170]'s fourth quadrant exactly. So the default is unclassified → indeterminate, never a silent pass, and an exhaustive test over the schema's own vocabulary fails the build when a new node or edge type lands with no class. Property changes on function-bearing nodes are indeterminate too: a reworded description may be a rename or a scope change, and the graph cannot tell — dec:three-party-checks says it counts and the human judges. What it deliberately does NOT claim: it compares two design records, so it says nothing about whether the code preserved function. Size M

Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-180 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: M.
